A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniUGG with the same authors, core architecture, and original experiments. The complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and redrawn material.

before.justification: V2 reports original encoder evaluations, spatial question-answering results, 3D generation experiments, and component ablations in Section 4 and Appendix A.3.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds 3D benchmark evaluations, separate-task optimization experiments, and qualitative robustness and failure analyses in Appendix A.3.

M1.justification: The core encoder, Spatial-VAE, LLM/diffusion architecture, and objectives are retained. Appendix A.3.2 newly applies a grounding refinement procedure on ScanRefer, with refined and unrefined results in Table 9. This is a limited procedural addition, although its implementation is unspecified.

E1.justification: V3 adds SQA3D and ScanQA scene question answering and ScanRefer text-guided 3D object localization, substantially extending evaluation coverage to grounding. It also adds extreme-view generation scenarios reaching 140 degrees. The previously evaluated datasets and tasks are retained.

E2.justification: New Table 9 adds comparisons with 3D-LLM, Chat-3D v2, LEO, LL3DA, Scene-LLM, LLaVA-3D, and Video-3D LLM, plus grounding comparators including ScanRefer, MVT, ViL3DRel, and Grounded 3D-LLM. Figure 11 newly compares feature matchings with MASt3R, explicitly distinguishing its access to the target image. Existing comparator sets remain intact.

E3.justification: V3 introduces supervised fine-tuning for the added 3D tasks, EM/BLEU-4/CIDEr and grounding accuracy evaluation, separate-task training controls, and tests at specified 60–140-degree rotations. Appendix A.2 also replaces the L2/SSIM weight listing with LPIPS and matching/RGB weights consistent with the existing equations; this revises reported settings without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations and simplified variant, v3 adds joint versus separate optimization (Table 10), grounding with versus without refinement (Table 9), feature matching (Figure 11), extreme-view generation (Figure 12), and color failure cases (Figure 13). These substantially expand analysis of task interference, geometric consistency, and failure conditions.

E5.justification: Both versions retain generation examples with different seeds, but neither reports benchmark repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added results follow the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–8 retain their values. New Table 9 reports UniUGG SQA3D EM of 51.3, ScanQA EM of 24.4, and ScanRefer Acc@0.25/0.5 of 23.2/7.8 without refinement versus 41.9/36.6 with refinement. Table 10 adds separate-training results, including VSI 42.2 for understanding-only versus 40.1 jointly trained. Figures 11–13 add correspondence and failure observations.

T1.justification: The mathematical representations, Equations 1–4, Spatial-VAE objective, and autoregressive VQA loss are retained. Neither version contains formal theorems or proofs, and v3 adds no substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: Both retain the first unified LLM-based 3D understanding/generation claim, geometric-semantic encoder and Spatial-VAE contributions, and the 17.9% relative VSI-Bench advantage claim. The additional evaluations and limitations do not redefine the principal contributions.

C2.justification: V3 substantially expands applicability qualifications: it acknowledges gaps against 3D-enhanced methods, explains extreme-view failures through training coverage and reduced overlap, and tentatively attributes color errors to competing encoder objectives. It also interprets separate-training results as an acceptable unification tradeoff and explicitly states missing language control, freeform editing, and interactive multi-round generation.

D1.justification: V3 adds training hardware and elapsed times, inference precision and latency, and training-pair filtering thresholds. It clarifies projector optimization, corrects loss-weight documentation, and removes the statement extending unified-training learning rates to VAE training. The code-release-upon-acceptance promise is deleted; the retained project link does not establish actual code availability.

R1.justification: V3 adds references supporting the new 3D benchmarks and comparison methods, including SQA3D, ScanRefer, Scene-LLM, and Video-3D LLM. Appendix A.3.2 extends positioning around 2D inputs and a 3B backbone versus 3D-enhanced methods. Section 2's research framing and the central novelty claim remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 adds a pipeline overview subsection, distinguishes the overall training stages from steps within unified training, expands appendix subheadings, and revises the conclusion into 'Conclusion and Limitations.' Conference headers and acknowledgments are added. Most existing prose and the overall section progression are retained.

P2.justification: V3 adds an overall pipeline diagram and combines the earlier separate training/inference explanations into a revised Figure 4. It adds Tables 9–10 and diagnostic Figures 11–13, and reformats retained visualization panels. The earlier simplified-variant Figures 11–12 survive as Figures 14–15; these are relocated material rather than new analyses.

improvement.justification: V3 addresses important gaps in v2's validation: Table 10 directly measures the performance tradeoff from joint training, Table 9 adds relevant 3D comparisons, and Figures 11–13 examine consistency and failure conditions. Together with clearer training explanations and resource disclosures, these substantially improve assessment of the central unification claim and its limits. The grounding refinement remains underdocumented, and claimed computational savings lack a direct separate-training cost comparison, but these limitations do not outweigh the gains.
